title: Largest plus smallest neighbour factor
why: Collatz-type: primes step +2, even n with n+1 prime grow up to 1.5x; ruling out infinite prime-driven chains out of reach. Cycles check.

title: Mixed divisor-sum map
why: Collatz-type sopf/P mix; primes grow via p+P(p+1); no contraction argument. Fixed points and cycles verified.

title: The parity-switch prime map
why: Odd primes n with (n-1)/2 prime grow 1.5x; Collatz-type global convergence. Nine-cycle through 5 verified by hand.

title: Factor plus next divisor-sum
why: Collatz-type; prime n gives n+sopf(n+1) growth up to ~1.5x; no potential function. Cycle (16,19,26) checks.

title: Square-sum Hamiltonian paths from 1
why: Weaker, start-restricted form of existing 'Counting square-sum chains' (leading growth of Hamiltonian path count).

title: Square-sum K4s
why: Four numbers with all pairwise sums square: Euler's parametric families (Guy, UPINT D15) give infinitely many with polynomially bounded ratio.

title: Permanent of the prime-sum matrix
why: Hankel 0-1 prime matrix, near-regular degree ~2n/log n; Bregman gives upper bound, matching lower bound needs pseudorandomness/scaling argument.

title: Optimal square-sum circle gaps
why: Trivial lower bound ~sqrt(N) from square gaps; O(sqrt N) upper needs Hamiltonian cycle in bounded-degree local reflection graph; constructive.

title: Continued fraction of the P-constant
why: Transcendence of a CF with non-automatic, non-repetitive unbounded quotients; no Adamczewski-Bugeaud-type method applies.

title: Two small factors and one large
why: Collatz-type; n, n+2 both prime gives ~2n growth (twin-prime-like chains); cycle through 16 checks.

title: The 2n+3 map
why: Collatz-type with growth via primes 2n+3 and n; climbs to 7 million show no simple contraction. Cycles verified.

title: The P(n)+P(n+2)−1 map
why: Collatz-type; twin primes n,n+2 give ~2n growth. Distinct from existing P(n)+P(n+2) item. Cycles (4),(223..469) verified.

title: Unbounded excursions in prime maps
why: Needs arbitrarily long chains of near-prime linear forms in one variable (Dickson-type); Maynard-Tao gives only some forms prime.

title: Prime-sum Kayles
why: Variant of existing square-sum Kayles; brute force N<=22 shows irregular outcomes (losses at 4,7,8,12,13,16,20), no evident pattern.

title: Large girth subgraphs of S_N
why: Girth-6 extremal number inside S_N (~N^1.5 edges); general bound N^{4/3}; true order unclear, needs square-sum structure.

title: Largest-factor tribonacci
why: Collatz-type; prime triple sums can grow ~3x; random starts reach 4 cycles, but no contraction proof possible.

title: Spanning-tree entropy of the spectre tiling
why: Limit exists by Lyons' tree-entropy theory for Folner patches; irrationality of h/Catalan has no method. Graph on patch slightly underspecified.

title: Matrices with prime entries and unit determinant
why: Parity forces an entry 2: count primes s with 2s+-1=qr; dominated by small q, i.e. twin-prime-type counts for r,(qr+-1)/2.

title: Prime Markov triples
why: Implies infinitely many prime Markov numbers (open; Bourgain-Gamburd-Sarnak only almost primes). Prime triples found: (2,5,29),(5,29,433),... heuristic borderline.

title: Seven-free Markov numbers
why: Markov numbers up to x number ~log^2 x, so digit heuristic predicts finitely many (172 of 6208 up to 10^80); likely false, unprovable.

title: Apollonian seven-free curvatures
why: Curvatures contain shifted binary quadratic form values; seven-free lower bound via Fourier decay of digit set, X^{o(1)} slack helps.

title: Largest factor of p² + p + 1 small
why: Dickman predicts density 1-log2; positive proportion at prime arguments needs equidistribution of Phi3 roots over primes (Hooley-Dartyge type).
